sections.title: Positioning
sections.summary: Clover sells a smart point-of-sale system to restaurants, retail, services and healthcare, with hardware as the centerpiece and a sales team as the main way in.
keyPoints: Homepage: 'A CLOVER FOR EVERY SMALL BUSINESS' and 'Do what you do better with the world's smartest POS system.'
Industry is the organising principle: full-service dining, quick-service restaurants, retail, professional, personal and home and field services.
The two homepage buttons are 'Get Clover' and 'Contact sales'; the contact page offers sales help rather than self-serve signup.

sections.title: Products and offerings
sections.summary: A POS software suite sold with a family of devices, plus payments, invoicing, capital and loyalty.

rows: Software for restaurants, retail and services, with customizable systems and online ordering
Go, Compact, Flex Pocket, Flex, Mini, Station Solo, Station Duo and Kiosk
In person, over the phone and online; invoicing and a Virtual Terminal
Rewards, promotions and open lines of communication with customers
Third-party apps for different business types

gaps: Device prices and individual plan prices were not on the surveyed pages.

sections.title: Pricing
sections.summary: Pricing is deliberately not shown as a list. The pricing page leads with one processing rate and an industry picker; plan details open per industry.
keyPoints: Headline rate: pay as little as 2.3% + 10¢ per transaction.
'Prices shown are only available on Clover.com' steers buyers to the online store rather than a sales rep.
An online-only offer gives a $450 statement credit when you buy a Station, Mini or Flex.
Six industry cards lead to per-industry plan comparisons; the Go page splits into Starter and Essentials.

rows: $450 statement credit on Station, Mini or Flex, online only
Compared per industry on separate pages; no plan prices in the surveyed text

gaps: Plan prices, device prices and subscription costs were not on the surveyed pages.

sections.title: Merchandising
sections.summary: The offer is merchandised by industry and by device with a promotional credit, and consultants fill the gap that the missing price list leaves. Merchants get loyalty, gift cards, online ordering and an app market.
keyPoints: An industry picker on the pricing page replaces a plan table.
A single low rate and a statement credit serve as the entry offer and anchor.
Business consultants are offered in person or by phone to pick a system.
For merchants: customer loyalty with rewards and promotions, gift cards, online ordering, analytics reports and an app market; one case study grew an inventory database to 15,000 items.

sections.title: Technical platform
sections.summary: A developer community with a partner program and an app market is advertised, but the surveyed pages give little technical detail.
keyPoints: Developer page invites visitors to create a global developer account and promotes featured partners.
An App Market lists apps by business need.
The Clover Connect link leads to a Fiserv page for software providers and ISVs about integrated payments.
gaps: API reference, SDKs and webhooks were not read.

sections.title: Design
sections.summary: Two voices: a dramatic, tightly condensed headline over restaurant photography on the home page, and a calm dark-green pricing page with white industry cards. Green and lime tie them together.
keyPoints: Home uses a heavy condensed typeface (Formula-Black) over a restaurant photo; the pricing page switches to altform; other pages use Graphik.
Greens carry the brand: #004400 and a lime (#b6fb6f) on the home page, a dark green hero (#012906) on pricing and a green promo bar.
Home opens with two buttons, black 'Get Clover' and lime 'Contact sales'.
The pricing page is a dark green hero with six white industry cards with icons.
The home page is 6,460px tall and the pricing page 5,385px.
gaps: Merchant design control was not shown in the surveyed pages.

sections.title: Company presentation
sections.summary: Small-business success stories carry the story, supported by large scale counters.
keyPoints: Case studies include 3X growth for a pizza restaurant, a 15% revenue increase from online ordering and a rewards program with 3,000+ loyal customers.
The home page has a 'Run the numbers' section on devices shipped, POS provider ranking and annualized processing volume.
Pages carry a Clover Network, LLC notice and a link to a Fiserv page.
gaps: No leadership or ownership information in the surveyed pages.

signupPath: No self-serve signup was found. The homepage offers 'Get Clover' and 'Contact sales'; the contact page is a sales form ('Get sales help'). The developer page has 'Create a Clover developer account', which was not followed. Nothing was entered.

jtbd_fit.evidence: Industry pages name the job (run a restaurant, retail or service business).

capability_visible.evidence: POS and device pages show features; no product demo or admin view.

pricing_transparency.evidence: One headline rate and a statement credit; plan and device prices are not shown.

product_breadth.evidence: Eight device models, POS by industry, payments, capital, loyalty and app market.

platform_depth.evidence: Developer community, partner program and app market, but little technical detail.

time_to_value.evidence: Capture stops before the product; first-value time was not observed.

friction.evidence: The surveyed pages could not tell.

mobile.evidence: Phone captures exist for home and pricing but were not assessed.

states.evidence: No error or empty states reached.

value_prop_clarity.evidence: 'A Clover for every small business' and 'smartest POS system' are clear about what is sold.

proof_quality.evidence: 'Smartest POS' is a superlative; case studies are specific.

persuasion_integrity.evidence: An online-only $450 credit carries an asterisk and 'prices shown are only available on Clover.com' pushes buyers online.

cta_logic.evidence: 'Get Clover' and 'Contact sales' sit side by side with no clear primary.

company_narrative.evidence: Small-business story is consistent; ownership and company background are not shown.

offer_packaging.evidence: Industry and device groupings help; plans are hidden behind per-industry pages.

offer_architecture.evidence: A low rate, a hardware credit and consultants, but no visible ladder.

merchant_merch_tools.evidence: Loyalty, promotions, gift cards, online ordering, analytics and an app market.

visual_craft.evidence: Strong photography and bold condensed type on home; a clean pricing hero.

system_coherence.evidence: Three typefaces across home, pricing and other pages, though greens tie them together.

merchant_design_control.evidence: The surveyed pages could not tell.

read.summary: A sales-led POS brand that hides plan prices behind industry pages and consultants. Strong on hardware and merchant tools, light on public pricing and technical detail.
pros: Industry-first navigation matches how owners think.
Eight devices are named and grouped.
Merchants get loyalty, gift cards, online ordering and an app market.
cons: Plan and device prices are not shown.
'Get Clover' and 'Contact sales' compete as primary actions.
The developer page has little technical detail.
read.howItSells: Sells a dependable, restaurant-grade system and a person to help: bold imagery, a low headline rate and an online-only credit.
copy: Offer an industry picker as the entry to pricing.
Pair hardware with a clear statement credit.
Use case studies with specific numbers.

hypothesis.statement: Showing one starter-plan price per industry on the pricing page will raise device-page clicks among visitors who would otherwise leave.
hypothesis.metric: Pricing-page click-through to a system page
hypothesis.decisionRule: Ship if click-through rises by a pre-agreed margin and sales close rate holds over four weeks.

merchandising.summary: Merchandised by trade and device, with a clear offer but a deliberately hidden price list.
pros: Industry picker in place of a plan table.
Statement credit as the entry offer.
Consultants offered in person or by phone.

design.summary: A confident, brand-led look with some variation in type between pages.
pros: Bold condensed type and restaurant photography make a strong first impression.
Green and lime make a recognisable brand.
cons: Two similar-weight buttons on the home hero.

claims.text: Do what you do better with the world's smartest POS system.
Out the Dough saw a 15% overall revenue increase with online ordering
Pay as little as 2.3% + 10¢ per transaction
